title: After the Mistake, Make Repair Possible | Parenting Rewind
audience_intent: Adults and parents; not directed to children
education_scope: General parenting education only; not personalised therapy, diagnosis, or medical advice.

narration.transcript: Your child knocks over a plant, and soil covers the floor. You are tempted to take away something completely unrelated. Pause. Once everyone is safe, connect the response to what actually happened. The plant needs care and the floor needs cleaning. Try: The soil spilled. Let us work out how to put this right. Keep the focus on repair, not character. Give your child a safe, manageable part, such as fetching a brush. Handle sharp pieces or other hazards yourself. Help where needed, then notice their contribution. A related response gives them a way to practise responsibility instead of only feeling bad.
